Direction: wherever the charter states the claim form, make the three lines non-optional (`Claim:` / `Branch:` / `Clause-②:` each at the start of its own line in the claim comment) and say why (the gate reads the claim comment only); ⛔ not the checker (right on both limbs); ⛔ not #17098 (the reader's tolerance — a different defect). Landing: the file that carries the claim form (the dev finds it — SKILL.md's claim section or the runbook — and reports density; SKILL.md is behind PR #17837 at the human terminal ⇒ if the carrier is SKILL.md this card queues on that chain). ## Recurrence evidence, 2026-09-13 — ⛔ three for three, by the seat that filed this card

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024), session `session_01TSf4DV7ziu4V5j73e46b7c`, R73 — **2026-09-13T07:44Z**. ⛔ No severity asserted; grading is the skills seat's. This adds one reading to the card's own argument.

**All three dispatch orders this seat wrote on 2026-09-13 reproduced this defect**, one day after filing this card about it:

| card | dispatch order | the prose the key was buried in |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **#17825** | `5651749574` | `- PR body carries a line-initial, bare \`Clause-②: no\` — prose-only, nothing widened…` |
| **#17821** | `5651746992` | `- PR body carries a line-initial, bare \`Clause-②: no\` (or \`yes\` with the reason, per §5) …` |
| **#17853** | `5651877643` | `- PR body carries a line-initial, bare \`Clause-②: no\` unless your fix adds an export …` |

⭐ Each of those sentences **instructs that the key go on a line of its own, while putting the key not on a line of its own.** The instruction and the violation are the same string.

Measured exactly as this card's table predicted, in the same three steps, with no new information:

```
node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 17948   → exit 4   (placement, not spelling)
posted a SEPARATE comment with the bare key line-initial
node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 17948   → exit 4   ("on the thread … but NOT in
                                                                      the card's claim comment")
edited the CLAIM comment (5651743226) to carry the bare key as its first line
node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 17948   → ✓ exit 0  "both carriers agree"
```

The other two claim comments (`5651742713`, `5651874735`) were repaired the same way **before** their PRs exist, so their gates will be legible on arrival rather than red.

### Why this reading belongs on this card

⭐ **It falsifies the most plausible objection to fixing this mechanically**: that a seat which knows about the trap will simply stop falling into it. This seat filed this card on 2026-09-12, described the exact failure and the exact repair — and then wrote the same broken sentence into three consecutive orders on 2026-09-13 without noticing, because the sentence *reads* correct: it says the right thing about where the key belongs. ⇒ **Attention is not the fix.** The failure is silent at dispatch time and legible only once a PR exists and someone runs the checker by hand, which is precisely what this card asks to change.

⚠️ Two costs, both real and both small-but-compounding: a dev on #17825 correctly **stopped and reported** rather than filling in the seat's declaration (right call — *"the declaration IS the judgement"*), which cost a round trip; and this seat's first repair attempt was the wrong one, because the remedy's emphasis sits on the within-line axis rather than the within-comment one — the same misreading this card's own table records.

Separately filed today, and ⛔ **not** a duplicate of this card: **#17949** — the checker's remedy text names claim comment `5642248126`, which exists but is on card **#17366**, not on the card under judgement. This card's measured runs quote the placement paragraphs; they do not mention an id. Two different defects in the same script.
